Privacy

Your words stay yours.

CommonCopy does its job locally. No account, no phrase uploads, and no background clipboard history.

01 / Local storage

Your phrases, categories, settings, and usage counts are stored as readable JSON on your computer. On Windows, that’s under your user profile in AppData. On Mac, it’s in Application Support. CommonCopy does not upload this file.

02 / Copy and paste

When you choose a phrase, CommonCopy places its text on the system clipboard and sends the paste shortcut. When you choose “Save highlighted text,” it sends the copy shortcut once and reads the selection into an editor. Previous plain text can be restored when the clipboard hasn’t changed in the meantime.

03 / Input access

Windows detects the configured Ctrl + right-click gesture and registered keyboard shortcut. Mac uses a mouse-only event tap and a registered shortcut. Accessibility permission is required on Mac for activation, capture, and paste. CommonCopy does not record typed text or continuously capture application content.

04 / This website

This preview has no cookies, analytics, tracking pixels, or advertising network scripts. Its interactive example uses temporary browser memory and does not upload text. The hosting provider processes standard website requests.

05 / Advertising

Third-party advertising is planned for the website only. No provider is connected yet. Provider information, relevant data practices, and any required choices will be added before advertising is enabled. The desktop utility stays ad-free.

06 / Sensitive information

CommonCopy is not encrypted secret storage. Keep passwords, authentication codes, recovery keys, and access tokens in a dedicated password manager. Export your library for a lasting backup; the automatic previous-version backup rotates.

Public release notes and support information will accompany the public downloads. Material changes will be reflected here.
